chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who bought a house that had an addition from the road. He said, 'If that was included in what he bought, there is no harm.'

key_terms.زِيَادَةٌ: An addition or extra space, often referring to an encroachment or extension beyond the standard boundaries.
key_terms.فِيمَا اشْتَرَى: Included in what was purchased; indicating the extra space was part of the sold property.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm; a legal term indicating validity or permissibility.

ai.seo_question: Is a house valid if it has an extra room built over the public street?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that an encroachment (*ziyadah*) into the public way does not invalidate a property sale if it was explicitly included in the agreed-up price and transfer of ownership. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle of *istishab* (presumption of validity) and the importance of contractual intent (*qasd*) in determining whether a defect warrants rescission (*khiyar al-ayb*). It highlights the flexibility in commercial transactions where minor structural irregularities are tolerated if they were part of the original agreement.
